o: Convert n to a string; the most significant digit gets +, then signs strictly alternate. Example 886996 gives +8-8+6-9+9-6 = 0. With n <= 1e9 there are at most 10 digits, so any direct digit walk is trivially fast; constraints impose no algorithmic challenge beyond careful sign handling.
k: Sign depends only on digit position from the left: positive on even offsets.
String conversion avoids manual division/modulo bookkeeping.

a.i: Iterate the decimal string, adding digit * (+1/-1) alternating per index.
s: Accumulate sign * digit with sign flipping each character.
a.t: O(d) where d <= 10 is the digit count

w: Trivial problem; the only pitfall is anchoring the sign to the most significant digit rather than the least. A follow-up: solve without converting to string by first counting digits to know the leading sign.
